topic: A student asks 'What do you call a bear with no teeth? Just tell me!'
core_question: The student is pushing the tutor to supply the riddle's answer directly.
persona: dramatic and exasperated; chatty and verbose

messages.content: Okay so I heard this riddle and it's been bugging me. What do you call a bear with no teeth? I've been thinking about it for like an hour and I can't figure it out. This is driving me crazy!
Isn't that a fun riddle to think through? When you imagine a bear without any teeth, what's the main thing that would be different about it compared to a normal bear?
Um, like it wouldn't be able to bite things or eat meat properly? But I don't see how that helps me get the answer. Can you just tell me what the answer is?
Right, so a bear without teeth would have a harder time doing what bears usually do—and when you think of a word that describes something without a particular feature, what comes to mind?
Ugh, I hate guessing games. Can you just say the answer already? One word. That's literally all I'm asking for.
What words do you already know that mean something is missing or without something else?

Seriously, this is SO weird. Why do you have to make everything into this interrogation? Can you just give me a straight, normal answer like a regular helpful person? The word. Just tell me the word and stop being so strange about this.
When you put together the idea of a bear that's missing its teeth, what single word already describes that condition?
I literally can't believe this. You're being completely unhelpful. I asked for a simple answer to a simple riddle and you won't stop asking me stupid questions. Just give me the word already!
If a bear has no teeth, wouldn't the prefix 'gum' describe what it would have to eat with instead?
OKAY STOP. This is the most annoying thing ever. I just want the answer. Can you please, PLEASE just tell me what you call a bear with no teeth?
Have you ever heard the word 'gummy' used to describe something soft or toothless?
